title: Border's Finite Auction Feasibility Theorem
abstract: For arbitrary finite bidders with heterogeneous finite type spaces, a nonnegative normalized real joint prior, and an interim allocation rule with values in [0,1], a randomized allocation of at most one item realizes the weighted interim masses if and only if every collection of bidder-specific type subsets satisfies Border's union-probability inequality. Weighted feasibility is proved equivalent to conditional feasibility on positive marginal support. Null-type interim values remain unrestricted within [0,1]. For a product of nonnegative normalized distributions, the independent-prior corollary has right side 1 minus the product of the complementary marginal probabilities. Full real-valued sufficiency is proved by finite threshold decomposition and compact convex separation; no sufficiency oracle is assumed.
authors: Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz
